  City Council Minutes
  October 6, 2025-5:00 P.M.
r-1  City Hall Council Chamber
  OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the regular meeting to order at 5:00 p.m.
  (Absent: Councilmember Madison)

  CLOSED SESSION  On the order of the Mayor, the regular meeting recessed at 5:00 p.m.
  to discuss the following closed session items:

  CONSIDERATION OF INITIATION OF LITIGATION pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4): One potential case

  CITY COUNCIL CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL
  regarding significant exposure to potential litigation pursuant
  to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2): One potential case

  The above closed session items were not discussed.

  On the order of the Mayor, the regular meeting reconvened at 6:03
  p.m. The pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Lyon.

  ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Rick Cole
  CouncilmemberTyron Hampton
  Councilmember Justin Jones
  Councilmember Jason Lyon
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda

  Staff:  City Manager Miguel Marquez
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

  CEREMONIAL MATTERS Eugene Harris, Police Chief, and Susana Porras, Pasadena Police
  Department Senior Communications Coordinator, introduced newly
  sworn in Pasadena Police Officers. The City Council welcomed the
  new officers and expressed gratitude for their serving the City.

  Mayor Gordo presented a proclamation declaring the month of
  October 2025 as Bullying Prevention Awareness Month and United
  Against Hate Week. Elliot Park, Pasadena youth member, and
  Sandy Greenstein, Human Relations Commissioner, thanked the
  City Council for the recognition and spoke on the importance of
  bullying prevention. Commissioner Greenstein also invited the City
  Council and the community to attend the Walk to Freedom event on
  Saturday, October 25, 2025.

  Council Minutes  1  10/06/2025
   Mayor Gordo issued a proclamation declaring October 2025 as
  Walktoberand Pedestrian Safety Month. Joaquin Siques, Director of
  Transportation, thanked the Mayor and City Council for the
  recognition and introduced Colin Bogart, from Day One, and Liz
  Schiller, from Pasadena Complete Streets Coalition, who invited the
  City Council and community members to participate in Walktober
  events, with various opportunities to explore the City on foot.

  Mayor Gordo requested that the meeting be adjourned in memory of
  Jane Goodall, an anthropologist and pioneer in primate ethology. He
  acknowledged her serving as the Grand Marshall of the 124th
  Tournament of Roses Parade in 2013, and her planned appearance
  on October 1, 2025 in Pasadena to launch TREEAMS, a student-led
  movement to plant over 5,000 trees in recent fire-ravaged areas.

  Councilmember Madison also requested that the meeting be
  adjourned in memory of Sidney Kirkpatrick, longtime Pasadena
  resident and bestselling author, and spoke on his contributions to
  Pasadena Central Library and system in 1993 by helping to promote
  and support the passage of the original Library Tax.

Council Minutes  4  10/06/2025
   Katie, San Gabriel resident, expressed concerns related to the
  Pasadena Police Department's budget for military equipment
  and heightened tensions in the community due to federal
1  immigration activities.

  Yadi, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns related to
  personal privacy and the Pasadena Police Department's use of
  drones.

  In response to Vice Mayor Rivas' inquiry regarding opportunities for
  feedback and input from the public and the Community Police
  Oversight Commission (CPOC) on the Police Department's Annual
  Military Equipment report, Anthony Russo, Police Lieutenant,
  confirmed that the report was presented at a community meeting, as
  well as to the CPOC, and neither had concerning comments. He also
  noted that City staff incorporated language requested by CPOC into
  the Military Equipment report.

  Vice Mayor Rivas advocated for the Police Department's policy to
  explicitly state that the sole purpose and authorized use of the .50
  caliber rifle is to disable vehicles being used in an attack scenario.

  Councilmember Cole advocated for future reports to be agendized
  for the City Council to review and offer feedback and
  recommendations to the Police Department.

  Councilmembers Hampton and Cole advocated for future reports to
  include a description of the feedback and recommendations
  provided by the CPOC to the City Council.

  Lieutenant Russo clarified that there is a procedural legal
  requirement that precludes the CPOC from making
  recommendations on the matter. Mayor Gordo also stated that while
  the information is presented to the CPOC and the public for
  transparency purposes, the City Council, as elected representatives
  of Pasadena, are singularly empowered with decision-making
  authority regarding Police equipment and other related public safety
  policies.

  MOTION:  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Masuda,
  seconded by Councilmember Madison, to approve the staff
  recommendation. (Motion unanimously approved) (Absent: None)

  City Manager Marquez provided introductory remarks on the item.

  In response to Councilmember Masuda's inquiry about additional
  soil testing efforts, Manuel Carmona, Public Health Director,
  reported that LA County coordinates a free soil-testing program that
  offers composite testing for people on private residential properties.
  He also reported that the County does publish the test results online.

  In response to Councilmember Madison's inquiry regarding persons
  impacted by lead and other fire-related pollutants, Public Health
  Director Carmona reported that Quest Diagnostics is providing free
  lead-detecting blood tests throughout the County. Councilmember
  Madison requested that the City test and monitor lead levels and
  impacts to first responders. He also advocated for the Public Safety
  Committee to receive a report addressing the City's and the County's
  after-action analysis.

  Katie, San Gabriel resident, expressed concerns regarding the
  City's evacuation response to the Eaton Fire.

  In response to public comment, Mayor Gordo reported that the City
  is schedule to recognize the members of the Job Center and
  supporters for their efforts in response to the Eaton Fire.

  Mayor Gordo suggested that the City monitor employees impacted
  by the Eaton Fire and provide additional testing opportunities, and to
  develop a heat map indicating where elevated levels of lead are
  being detected so that the City may conduct additional outreach and
  testing for residents.

  required public outreach, Transportation Director Siques reported
  that public outreach is required by the funding agency and by the
  City's own process.

  Councilmember Madison expressed concerns that the required
  outreach component may block necessary projects from moving
  forward given that the outreach must indicate the need for the
  projects. He also advocated to give more weight to local vendors in
  the bidding process.

  Councilmember Cole advocated for the City to enhance consistency

  community engagement services for the City, and to provide
  centralized staff support for public engagement rather than
